newsitem.title: FINLAND: ENSO SEES '97 EARNINGS SIMILAR TO '96.
newsitem.headline: ENSO SEES '97 EARNINGS SIMILAR TO '96.

text.p: Enso Group, set to be Europe's second largest forestry firm after a German acquisition, said on Tuesday it expected 1997 earnings to be similar to the 1996, when it made a 1.7 billion markka profit after financial items.
"The group's financial result for 1997 is likely to be similar to that for 1996," the company said in a statement with its Q1 1997 report.
"The strengthening of short-fibre market pulp prices in the past few weeks will make it easier to raise paper prices. Prices are expected to rise during the second half of the year," Enso said.
Enso repeated earnings and cash flow would be boosted by its acquisition this year of 50.4 percent of German paper-maker E. Holtzmann & Cie AG for 1.8 billion markka.
"The deal will improve the group's per-share cash flow immediately and earnings per share as the synergy benefits materialise," Enso said.

Its majority Holtzmann holding was consolidated on April 28, Enso said. "The acquisition's effect on the group's equity-to- assets ratio is cushioned by the fact that the (Enso) group does not intend to make any decisions for significant new investments for 1998," it said.
"(Pulp) stocks began to fall during March and prices have started to strengthen going into the second quarter," Enso said.
"Increases are anticipated in market pulp prices, which could lead to increases in fine paper prices," Enso said.
"Demand for office papers is still growing at about two percent a year, and the market for these grades is more in balance than for graphic papers," it said.
Enso said that despite the "favourable market" for newsprint, prices had not yet begun to rise.
"Improving economic prospects on the (book paper) division's main markets are expected to strengthen demand and lead to price rises during the second half of the year," Enso said.
"(Corrugated board) prices are expected to rise during the summer," it said.
